fields.meta_title: Beta Landing Page Builder for Tester Signups | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Create a beta landing page that recruits testers, caps seats by platform, and collects bug reports. See four working examples. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Beta Landing Page That Recruits Real Testers
fields.hero_description: Build a beta landing page that limits tester seats, asks screening questions, and keeps each signup in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Beta Page
fields.features_subheading: A beta landing page has one job: find testers who will use the product and say what broke. These six parts do that job.
fields.feature_1:
A pitch that says what testers get

Describe the product, who the beta is for and what testers receive. Emergent builds the page around it: the promise, the start date, the time you ask of testers, and the form.
fields.feature_2:
Screening questions on the form

Ask what a good tester has in common: the phone they carry, the tool they use now, how often they hit the problem. Each answer saves as a column you can sort and filter by.
fields.feature_3:
Seat counts that change as people join

Set a cap for the cohort, or one cap per platform. The page shows how many seats are left and updates the count as testers sign up, so a full group closes on its own.
fields.feature_4:
Every applicant in a table you own

Each signup becomes a row with its answers, the link it came from, and a status. Mark testers accepted or held, and the app emails each group the message you wrote for it.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts in Slack and email

A booked kickoff call or a blocker bug can post to Slack or arrive by email. The app connects to any tool with an API, so accepted testers can also sync to your CRM.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and code you can keep

Publish on an address like beta.yourapp.com; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans also add full code export to your own GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every iPhone seat is taken, and Android has 12 left

Plover opens 60 tester seats on its habit tracker's beta page, 30 for iPhone and 30 for Android, and the count updates as testers sign up. iPhone filled first. Android has 18 of 30 seats taken, Ximena Florin's among them, and the page now offers only that option. Each tester's phone and OS version save to the testers table.
fields.tab_content_2:
The first build goes to the 31 who booked a call

Wickmoor, a route planner for landscaping crews, ends its beta signup with a 20-minute kickoff call slot. Applicants who book a call get the first build, and the rest get an email reminder. Of 74 applicants, 31 booked, Baptiste Riaz of Gorsefield Lawn Care among them, and 43 got the reminder.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 188 riders who qualified, 100 get a test light

Skiff has 100 test lights, and its beta page asks each applicant how many times a week they ride. Riders who answer 3 or more qualify. The first 100 of them by signup time get a light, Ludmila Pelling among them, and the other 88 of the 188 who qualified wait as reserves.
fields.tab_content_4:
Blocker bugs post to Slack, 6 of them in week 3

Velmont, an invoicing app for photographers, gives each accepted tester a bug report form with a severity field. Every report lands in the app's dashboard, and reports marked Blocker also post to the #beta-bugs Slack channel. In week 3, testers filed 57 reports and 6 were blockers, one of them from Radko Valka.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Beta Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a beta landing page around the testers you want, then build and publish it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide who the beta is for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the trade in plain terms
fields.howto_step_1_des: Before writing any copy, name the tester you want in one line, such as crews of five or more or riders out 3 times a week, and turn that line into the screening questions on the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down what a tester gets and what you ask in return: early access or a free unit, against a weekly survey or a 20-minute call. Put both near the signup form. Applicants should know the deal before they apply.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick a seat count you can talk to in the first two weeks, and split it by platform or plan if that matters. A visible count of seats left shows visitors the beta is real and has a limit.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the tester profile, the trade, and the seat count into Emergent as one prompt. It builds the page, the form with your screening questions, and the testers table, and you change any part of it by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose what happens after each kind of signup. Accepted testers get the welcome email and the first build; held testers get a note about when the next group opens. Add a Slack or email alert for the applicants worth a call.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Sign up as a tester yourself
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run two test signups on a phone and a laptop, once with answers that qualify and once with answers that do not. Check that both emails arrive, both rows land in the table, and the seat count moves.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page on its own address, such as beta.yourapp.com, and post the link where likely testers already gather, like your newsletter or an in-app banner. Watch the testers table through the first day and answer early questions fast.

faq_plan.q: What is a beta landing page?
faq_plan.a: A beta landing page is a page that recruits testers for a product before its public release. It explains what the beta is, who it is for, and what testers get, then collects signups through a short form. Unlike a plain email list, it can screen applicants and cap the number of seats.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a beta landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the product, the testers you want, and the seat count in one prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It builds the page, the signup form with its screening questions, and a table for every applicant. Run two test signups of your own, then publish the page on your domain.

faq_plan.q: What should a beta signup landing page tell testers?
faq_plan.a: A beta signup landing page should tell testers what the product does, who the beta is for, what they get, and what you ask of them in return. Add the start date and the number of seats. Name the time it takes in plain numbers, such as one 20-minute call a week.

faq_plan.q: How long should a beta interest form be?
faq_plan.a: Keep a beta interest form to an email address and two or three screening questions. Ask only what decides who gets in, such as their phone platform or the size of their crew. If all you need is a line of names before launch, a waitlist landing page is the simpler build.

faq_plan.q: Should a beta signup form ask testers to commit to giving feedback?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put the commitment on the beta signup form as a checkbox and name the task exactly, such as a weekly 3-question survey or one kickoff call. A tester who ticked a specific task knows what is expected, and the app can mark anyone who has not done it yet.

faq_plan.q: How many testers should a beta landing page accept?
faq_plan.a: Accept only as many testers as you can hear from in the first round, then open more seats in later groups. Set that number as a cap on the page, and the app counts the seats left and closes the form when the group is full. Emergent puts no response caps on the form itself; the only limit is yours.

faq_plan.q: When should I put up a beta landing page?
faq_plan.a: Put up a beta landing page once testers can use a build within a few weeks of signing up. Before that, a coming soon page that collects emails is the better fit, and you can invite that list when the beta opens.

faq_plan.q: How do testers get the build after signing up on a beta landing page?
faq_plan.a: Testers get the build through each platform's own test program. For an iPhone app, Apple's TestFlight lets you invite up to 10,000 external testers to join your beta program, once you have your first build already approved by App Review for TestFlight. For Android, a Google Play closed test can use lists of testers by email address.

faq_plan.q: Can a beta landing page collect bug reports from testers?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give accepted testers a report form on the page that asks for the steps, a screenshot, and a severity. In an app built with Emergent, each report saves to a database you own, and the app can post the most serious ones to a Slack channel or send them by email.

faq_plan.q: Can a service business run a beta landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A beta can test a new service as well as software, such as a gym trying a class format or a clinic piloting evening hours with existing patients. Give the pilot its own page with a seat cap, and link to it from the main site, the way a chiropractic landing page might point regulars to an evening-hours trial.

plan.angle: The live SERP for beta landing page is an example gallery SERP (Dribbble, Pure Landing, One Page Love's waitlist and beta section, a Reddit examples thread, an Indie Hackers before and after) plus one best-practices post, an AI Overview and related searches for templates, examples and early access designs. The galleries stop at screenshots. This page treats a beta page as a tester recruiting page, not a queue: it shows four working beta pages built from a prompt, each with the logic behind the form: seats capped per phone platform, a kickoff call that decides who gets the first build, test units given to riders who qualify, and a bug report form that posts blockers to Slack. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, what the page should tell testers, form length, a feedback commitment, how many testers to accept, timing, getting builds to testers on iOS and Android (sourced to Apple and Google), bug reports and service pilots. Waitlist queues, coming soon pages, product launches and startup pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Beta Landing Page That Recruits Real Testers'; hero 'Build a beta landing page that limits tester seats, asks screening questions, and keeps each signup in a database you own.' covers the whole recruiting job, no sibling topic.

intent.evidence: Example-gallery SERP answered with four working examples (Mobile App Beta, Closed B2B Beta, Hardware Beta, Tester Feedback), a 7-step how-to and a definition up top for the AI Overview.

specificity.evidence: Beta vocabulary throughout: 'Seat counts that change as people join', 'Screening questions on the form', TestFlight and Google Play closed tests in FAQ 8.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Plover opens 60 tester seats...', 'Skiff has 100 test lights...', 'Describe the product, who the beta is for...'.

craft.evidence: Two ', so' endings (feature_3, feature_5) recorded as a note; otherwise one idea per sentence.

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous detail: '#beta-bugs Slack channel', 'Baptiste Riaz of Gorsefield Lawn Care', 'a 20-minute kickoff call slot'.

truth.evidence: TestFlight 10,000 external testers and App Review condition match developer.apple.com/testflight quotes; 'a Google Play closed test can use lists of testers by email address' keeps the source's 'can create lists' scope. Claims map to claims_used ids. Numbers add up: 30+30=60, 18 taken/12 left, 31+43=74, 100+88=188, 6 of 57.

distinct.evidence: Waitlist and coming soon are framed as the other builds ('If all you need is a line of names before launch, a waitlist landing page is the simpler build'; 'Before that, a coming soon page that collects emails is the better fit'); no sibling primary in a heading; developer page's Quillrun beta tab is a dev-tool audience, no tab or story shared with this page; startup and product-launch mention beta only in passing.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first, hub link in item 2, sibling links to waitlist landing page, coming soon page and chiropractic landing page (all real pages); secondaries 'beta signup landing page', 'beta interest form', 'beta signup form' each worked in once; moat line in FAQ 6 'Emergent puts no response caps on the form itself'.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches copy: iPhone 30 of 30, Android 18 of 30, '12 Android seats left'; '31 of 74 booked, 43 email reminders sent'; '100 lights assigned, 88 reserves of 188'; '6 blockers, 57 reports in week 3', Blocker from Radko Valka in #beta-bugs. One hero, readable text.
